steps.tx: **Copper enzymes** span several systems at once. Ceruloplasmin is a ferroxidase that loads iron onto transferrin, directly linking copper to iron handling. Lysyl oxidase crosslinks collagen, cytochrome c oxidase finishes the respiratory chain, dopamine beta-hydroxylase makes noradrenaline, and copper zinc superoxide dismutase disposes of superoxide radicals. One metal, five examinable jobs, is the efficient way to store this list.
steps.say: Copper runs iron loading, collagen crosslinking, respiration, noradrenaline and antioxidant defence. Learn those five jobs and copper questions become straightforward.

steps.tx: **Wilson disease** is copper export failure. The ATP7B transporter normally loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes surplus into bile; when it fails, copper accumulates in liver, basal ganglia and cornea. Kayser-Fleischer rings, wing beating tremor, dysarthria and liver disease form the clinical picture, usually presenting between childhood and early adult life.
steps.say: Wilson disease traps copper in liver, brain and cornea because ATP7B cannot export it. Wing beating tremor with liver disease in a young person is the clue.

steps.tx: **Wilson tests and treatment** need their caveats stated. Ceruloplasmin is usually low but can be normal in about a fifth of patients, so a normal result never excludes the disease; urinary copper runs high instead. Penicillamine chelates copper for removal, while zinc blocks gut copper uptake by inducing metallothionein, an elegant treatment pairing of removal plus blocked entry.
steps.say: Ceruloplasmin can be normal in Wilson disease, so do not exclude it on that alone. Penicillamine removes copper while zinc blocks its entry.

steps.tx: **Menkes disease** is the mirror image transporter failure. ATP7A normally exports copper from gut cells into blood; when it fails, copper stays trapped in the gut wall and the whole body starves despite adequate intake. Babies develop kinky, depigmented, steel wool hair, severe neurological decline and connective tissue weakness, tragically opposite to Wilson overload in every direction.
steps.say: Menkes is Wilson in reverse: copper cannot leave the gut, so the body starves. Kinky pale hair with neurological decline in an infant is the signal.

steps.tx: **Zinc functions** centre on gene expression and repair. Hundreds of enzymes use zinc, and zinc finger domains let transcription factors grip DNA, so growth, taste, smell, immunity and wound healing all suffer early in deficiency. Acrodermatitis enteropathica, an inherited uptake transporter defect, gives the memorised picture: periorificial and acral rash, hair loss and diarrhoea in a weaning infant.
steps.say: Zinc fingers grip DNA, so deficiency hits growth, taste, immunity and healing together. Rash around openings with hair loss and diarrhoea is the inherited form.

steps.tx: **Excess zinc poisons copper** through the same metallothionein trick used therapeutically. Chronic high zinc intake, classically from denture adhesive creams swallowed over years, induces gut metallothionein that traps dietary copper in shed enterocytes. The result is an iatrogenic copper deficiency with anaemia and spinal cord neurology mimicking B12 deficiency, cured by stopping zinc and replacing copper.
steps.say: Too much zinc traps copper in the gut and manufactures copper deficiency, anaemia and cord signs included. Ask about denture cream when the story fits.
